newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures close lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures close lower.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures closed lower, as the dollar's correction proved light and short-lived.
"Clearly, the dollar was well bid," one currency trader said.

March marks managed to rebound to $0.5953 in the closing minutes of pit trade, but the contract remains well-entrenched in its bearish trend. Several traders attributed gains in mark futures to ongoing concerns about the EMU, which supported cash marks against most currencies.
"Lira just got crushed," one trader said.

Juergen Stark, a senior German finance ministry official, said that he knew of no plans aimed at trying to keep Italy out of the first group of nations to participate in the planned single European currency.

A Belgian newspaper quoted Belgium central bank governor Alfons Verplaestse as saying that the EMU would best start without Italy as the country would not be able to meet EMU criteria. Verplaestse denied his remarks were about Italy.
However, several traders said there were underlying market concerns that neither Germany nor Italy would meet the European Monetary Union requirements.
Such concerns highlighted by Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi's comments on Monday, which helped prop the U.S. currency higher, several currency traders said.

Prodi, who was visiting Germany on Monday, said Germany lacked the political commitment to the EMU. Prodi also said that Germany's leadership was failing to take action needed to shape up its economy for the launch of the EMU in 1999.
While some traders thought Prodi's comments were inappropriate, others agreed with Prodi's assessment on Germany's commitment to the EMU.
Stark repeated on Tuesday that in 1997 Germany would meet the Maastricht deficit criteria.
"People are a bit nervous and confused," one futures trader said.
However, he expects March marks to slink back through $0.5926, or about 1.6900 spot marks, in the very near term.
March yen inched up to $0.008108, just shy of testing resistance at $0.008109 or 123.75 spot yen.
While traders believe March yen will dip to $0.008029 or 125.00 before Japan's fiscal year-end on March 31, many are uncertain whether spot will hold above 125.00 after March 31.
AT 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Wednesday, the U.S. December international trade data and the U.S. January Consumer Price Index (CPI) will be released.

At the end of pit trade, March yen was up $0.000022 to $0.008104, marks were up $0.0010 to $0.5948, Swiss francs were $0.0031 lower at $0.6819, sterling was off $0.0144 to $1.6056, Canadian dollars were down $0.0028 to $0.7390, Australian dollars eased $0.0008 to $0.7649, and Mexican pesos were off $0.000375 to $0.126750.
